headline: Profit rises as financing revenue outpaces higher costs
summary_short: Q2 revenue rose 8.8% q/q and 9.8% y/y to $2,286M as net income climbed to $410M (+16.5% y/y); diluted EPS reached $1.18, up from $1.04 a year ago.
summary_long: Net income rose to $410M (basic EPS $1.19, diluted $1.18) on higher net financing revenue and other interest income and stronger other revenue, partially offset by higher noninterest expense and a $46M increase in the provision for credit losses tied to consumer-auto portfolio growth. Automotive Finance segment pretax income fell to $410M from $472M on higher interest expense and provision, while Insurance and Corporate Finance both grew. CET1 ratio held at 10.15%, net interest margin expanded to 3.59% from 3.41%, and total deposits reached $154.0B. The company repurchased $148M of common stock and paid a $0.30/share dividend; cash fell to $7.84B on loan growth and preferred-stock refinancing.

drivers.explanation: Increase was primarily driven by higher net financing revenue and other interest income and higher total other revenue, partially offset by higher noninterest expense and higher provision expense.
Net financing revenue rose $168M on higher average earning assets and lower interest expense from lower benchmark rates; insurance premiums grew on higher GAP and other F&I volume.
Provision for credit losses rose $46M on consumer-automotive portfolio growth, partially offset by lower net charge-offs; noninterest expense rose $57M on higher compensation and operating expenses.
EPS growth slightly outpaced net income growth after the 0.4% y/y reduction in weighted-average diluted shares from buybacks.
